description: A group of college friends looking to have fun while learning through a hackathon.
summary: Space Survivors is a bilingual (English/Portuguese), mobile-first educational decision-card game where young players command a lunar south pole base for 10 days using real 2024–2025 solar storm and astronomical data from NASA. By balancing oxygen, solar power, radiation exposure, and scientific research—supported by custom pixel-art visuals, an animated lunar diorama, and an adaptive procedural soundtrack—players learn how real space weather and lunar environment constraints shape Artemis-era exploration.
details:
How It Works & Pedagogical Design

Designed for young learners ("Junior Astronauts") on phones, tablets, and desktops, the game turns complex heliophysics and lunar engineering trade-offs into intuitive swipe, tap, or keyboard (← / →) choices:

  • 10-Day Lunar South Pole Loop: Each day progresses through five structured phases:
    1. Shift Start (Solar Illumination): Low-angle sunlight at the lunar south pole casts long crater and mountain shadows, yielding 0, 1, or 2 units of solar power per day.
    2. Life Support: Players manage oxygen generation (electrolysis, air purifiers, CO₂ scrubbers, greenhouse lighting) against crew consumption (2 air units every night).
    3. Scientific Research (Inside vs. Outside): Players choose between indoor research (studying regolith samples or observing the Sun with a telescope, which costs power) and Extra-Vehicular Activities (EVAs—driving the rover to craters or collecting polar ice, which yields science with lower power cost but exposes the crew to radiation).
    4. Dynamic & Real Astronomical Events: Days conclude with equipment maintenance problems, supply opportunities, real dated astronomical events, or incoming solar particle storms.
    5. Night Cycle: The crew consumes oxygen and accumulates baseline radiation (+1% per night) from galactic cosmic rays and the solar wind.
  • 40 NASA Discoveries & In-Game Discovery Terminal: Completing research unlocks 40 real scientific facts organized into four domains (Regolith & Lab, Craters & Rover, Polar Ice & Water, and Sun & Radiation). Each card explains both the scientific finding and its operational impact on a lunar base ("At the base"), stored persistently in a multi-window Discovery Terminal accessible during and between missions.
  • Spaced-Repetition Memory Quizzes: A few days after unlocking a discovery, a bonus quiz card tests the player's recall with an animated suspense sequence, streak combos, and Air/Power rewards—or a direct shortcut to review the report in the Discovery Terminal if they miss.
  • Personalized Post-Mission Debrief: At mission end (victory or early return to Earth due to air, power, or radiation limits), a 3-point telemetry debrief highlights what went well, specific areas to improve, and a chronological log comparing the player's actions against official NASA event records.
  • Guided Onboarding: Includes an 11-screen animated visual tutorial (#guide) and a full reference manual (#tutorial) whose values dynamically reflect the game's simulation parameters.

Visuals, Custom Assets & Adaptive Audio

  • Custom Pixel-Art Assets (assets/hud/): Hand-crafted pixel-art HUD indicators (oxygen tank SVG gauge, power, radiation, science flask, sound controls, and panoramic base art) paired with a custom pixel-icon renderer (assets/hud/pixel-icons.js).
  • Interactive Lunar Diorama (assets/scene/lunar-scene.js): A live HTML5 Canvas (256×88 upscaled crisp pixel art) rendering the lunar south pole base, shifting solar shadows, astronaut movement, rover crater expeditions, lunar eclipses, meteor showers, and solar particle storms impacting the base's radiation shield—plus an automated camera director on the home screen.
  • Procedural Music & Dynamic Soundscape (Web Audio API + assets/audio/): An original, copyright-free procedural music synthesizer generates a calm kalimba-and-chord lunar score that dynamically shifts in real time into a tense bass/pulse arrangement whenever solar alerts, EVAs, or meteor showers occur. Procedural sound effects accompany every swipe, meter change, storm impact, and quiz reveal, with automatic music ducking during voice/shelter alerts (assets/audio/corrida-queda.mp3).

NASA Data, Pipeline (datas/ & tools/) & Scientific Simplifications

Following NASA Space Apps guidelines on scientific transparency and data attribution:

  • 32 Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) Storms (2024–2025)
    • Source & Implementation: NASA CCMC DONKI via api.nasa.gov, stored in datas/ and processed by tools/build-storms.mjs and tools/embed-storms.mjs.
    • Role in the Game: Uses real UTC arrival timestamps, M/X flare classes, CME speeds (km/s), and real warning lead times (warn in minutes) to determine if the player gets an early flare alert (90% shelter shield) or an unwarned/fast arrival (50% emergency shield).
    • Source & Implementation: NASA Science (Eclipses), NASA DONKI (May 14, 2024 X8.7 flare), and NASA Meteor Watch (Geminids & Quadrantids).
    • Role in the Game: Triggers historical lunar eclipses (cutting solar power), major solar flares, and micrometeorite dust showers on their corresponding mission days.
    • Source & Implementation: NASA Missions — Apollo, LRO, LCROSS, SOFIA, Lunar Prospector, SDO, Parker Solar Probe, and ISS research.
    • Role in the Game: Powers the 40 collectible discoveries in the Discovery Terminal, each linked directly to its official NASA reference page.
    • Source & Implementation: Node.js simulation suite in tools/sim.mjs.
    • Role in the Game: Runs automated Monte Carlo playthroughs against the decoupled Engine module to verify resource balance, storm survivability, and educational pacing.

Scientific Simplifications & Disclosures:

  • Offline Pre-Cached Dataset: All NASA DONKI and astronomical records were downloaded, deduplicated (events within 48 hours merged into single storm episodes), and embedded into the build via tools/ so the game runs reliably offline without API rate limits or network failures.
  • Game Abstractions vs. Engineering Units: Air, power, and radiation meters use simplified integer scales rather than engineering units (such as kWh, kPa, or mSv). The base "shield" represents a thick-walled regolith/water radiation storm shelter, and each discovery abstracts In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) and mission science operations.

Technical Architecture, Accessibility & Child Safety

  • Zero-Dependency Architecture: Built purely with semantic HTML5, CSS3, and modular vanilla JavaScript, cleanly separating the pure-logic Engine from the DOM interface and LunarScene renderer.
  • Accessibility: Full support for touch swipe, pointer click, and keyboard navigation (←, →, Esc, Tab focus trapping), ARIA live regions, and automatic animation simplification when prefers-reduced-motion is enabled.

Child Safety: All external links to official NASA pages (ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov, science.nasa.gov, nasa.gov) are intercepted by a modal warning dialog alerting young players—and advising adult supervision—before opening external websites.


Use of Super Intelligence (SI)

During the development of Space Survivors, our team used generative AI assistants (ChatGPT and Gemini) as productivity, coding, and pedagogical-design tools, while keeping all scientific data, game logic, and creative assets under strict human and programmatic verification:

  • Pedagogical Framing & Bilingual Localization (PT/EN): AI tools assisted in brainstorming clear, age-appropriate phrasing for young learners and refining the bilingual Portuguese/English copy across the 11-screen visual tutorial (#guide), the full reference manual (#tutorial), the 40 NASA discovery reports (DISC), and the 40 spaced-repetition memory quizzes (DISC_QUIZ).
  • Code Refactoring, Procedural Audio & Automated Testing: AI supported refactoring the JavaScript architecture so that the core game rules (Engine) remain completely decoupled from the DOM interface and the HTML5 Canvas lunar diorama (LunarScene). It also assisted with responsive mobile-first CSS adjustments, procedural Web Audio synthesis (the adaptive kalimba/tension soundtrack and sound effects), and Node.js scripts in tools/—including the storm data pipeline (tools/build-storms.mjs, tools/embed-storms.mjs) and the headless game-balance simulator (tools/sim.mjs).
  • Strict Scientific Verification (No AI-Generated Data): No AI-generated space-weather or astronomical records were used in the project. Every UTC timestamp, solar flare class, Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) speed, and warning lead time for the 32 Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) storms and 6 dated astronomical events was extracted directly from official NASA DONKI (api.nasa.gov) and NASA Science records, stored in datas/, and verified programmatically. All 40 scientific facts were manually checked against and linked directly to official NASA mission pages (Apollo, LRO, LCROSS, SOFIA, Lunar Prospector, SDO, Parker Solar Probe, and ISS).
  • Original Visual & Audio Assets: All pixel-art HUD elements (assets/hud/), scene sprites (assets/scene/), and audio assets (assets/audio/) were produced or assembled specifically for this project without unverified copyrighted material.
